candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a). This is a renewal of an existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 is governed by the reissued permit versus the prior permit affects which effluent limits and monitoring conditions are in force for that period.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 require that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The choice among technology-based guidelines, WQBELs (numeric or narrative), and prior-permit limits determines which enforceable limit applies to each parameter; narrative WQBELs also affect whether an ordinary numeric measurement can be compared for compliance.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigning TSS to a technology-based basis rather than a WQBEL basis changes which limit derivation rules and associated monitoring framework apply to TSS measurements in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifying pH and TRC as WQBEL-driven parameters affects the applicable limit values, the monitoring obligations tied to those parameters, and how missing or non-numeric results should be interpreted when compliance comparison may not be numeric.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require technology-based effluent limitations to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an ELG applies versus BPJ (or a combination) determines the derivation path and resulting numeric technology-based limits for parameters such as TSS.

candidates.exact_span: In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If no promulgated ELG applies, BPJ becomes the operative basis for technology-based numeric limits, changing which values govern compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: EPA establishes limitations based on the following technology-based controls: BPT, BCT, and BAT.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which technology level (BPT, BCT, or BAT) governs a given pollutant determines the applicable technology-based effluent limit used in compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: BCT - Technology-based standard for the discharge from existing industrial point sources of conventional pollutants including BOD, TSS, fecal coliform, pH, and O&G.
candidates.computation_change_reason: BCT explicitly covers TSS and pH; interpreting whether BCT (versus BPT or BAT) applies to those parameters could change the technology-based limit selected, especially where the segment elsewhere assigns pH to WQBELs.

candidates.exact_span: BAT - The most appropriate means available on a national basis for controlling the direct discharge of toxic and non-conventional pollutants to navigable waters. BAT effluent limits represent the best existing performance of treatment technologies that are economically achievable within an industrial point source category or subcategory.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If TRC or other parameters are interpreted as toxic or non-conventional rather than solely WQBEL-driven, BAT could become the governing technology basis and alter the applicable numeric limit.
